root_causes: The Preview 4 screenshot records HTTP 502 during DR24 acquisition, but does not identify the underlying network or source failure.

The Windows CI live DR24 smoke passed for the bounded single- and multi-OID requests. This shows the tested HATS route works in that CI environment, but it does not establish why the user's machine received HTTP 502.
The Windows build stopped at Ruff formatting before the frozen application, GUI smoke, installer, and checksum stages.
The cumulative lifecycle gate requires a machine-readable cycle record for meaningful pull requests; PR #323 did not yet contain one at the time of the failed run.

findings: A live API smoke test on CI does not replace reproduction on the user's target Windows device.
Do not report requested OIDs as missing when source acquisition fails. Membership remains unknown until a successful source response supports an accounting decision.
Source reachability and API acquisition success do not establish scientific benchmark validity.
A green Scientific Validation contract workflow is not equivalent to a verified scientific release gate.
A Windows installer is not ready until the exact-head workflow passes packaging, frozen self-test, real WebView2 GUI smoke, install/uninstall, and checksum steps.
